<div>
![](../../src/images/hex_complex.png){.intro_image}

We will be using **iteration** quite heavily throughout the remainder of this course. As such, we thought it might be good to include a video that reviews iteration applications that are frequently used with spatial data. We do not break new ground here! In completing this lesson, you should develop a solid grasp on how to use iteration with `purrr::map()` to reduce repetition in shapefile operations, including:

* Reading in and pre-processing
* Joining
* Plotting

You will also get an opportunity to review many of the shapefile operations that we have used in this class thus far!

**Important!** Before starting this tutorial, be sure that you have completed all preliminary and previous lessons.

</div>

## Video content

In this lesson, you will code along with the script file [purrr_applied.R]{.mono} -- this file should be located in the [scripts]{.mono} folder of your project directory. 

Before you begin, please note:

* Your [purrr_applied.R]{.mono} file may look slightly different than the one used in the video tutorial. Your version of the file has been updated to adhere to the course style guide. I have also included the script file [purrr_applied_key.R]{.mono} so you can see the script in more modern code styling (but please do not peak until after you have completed all of the challenges!).
* I attach the *lubridate* library at the start of this session. The *lubridate* package is now part of the **core tidyverse** and thus does not need to be explicitly attached.
* I use single rather than double quotes in the video. The latter is my current preference.
* My indentation is off at several points.
